doc.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016

title: His tune 'Country' and Mark Hatch
summary: A clip of his tune 'Country', inspired by the farm road near Prospect, played by friend Mark Hatch.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: All right. Let me play this.
Oh I know what this is. Yeah that’s my good friend Mark Hatch.
I love that change right there.
And extended beyond where you thought. I love that.

That’s a little tune I wrote called “Country.” And I was actually thinking about where I grew up, just outside of Prospect. We had a half mile dirt road from where the bus would drop us off to where our farm was. And I walked down that road many times. And one morning I was just kind of thinking about that and I heard this little melody and these changes, and sketched it out and had this little tune. And one day, Mark Hatch is one of my dearest, dearest best friends. Tremendous flugelhorn/trumpet player. He was busy on the L.A. scene, played with Ray Charles, played with Chaka Khan and Rufus, actually Mark got me on Chaka’s gig. And one of the finest players ever. He kind of left the business a long time ago but he never put down the horn. And he has a great jazz group called Route Five, which I played in and still play in from time to time. But I thought okay, let’s bring this into rehearsal, and I just wanted to hear it. And the guys played it and it was wonderful. So we did this at a little songwriter night and he was kind enough to come play with me.
